contradictions.what: Rep said there was nothing they couldn't show and it was clean, but later admitted dancing around PayPal and having no crisp Venmo answer.
Rep said 'clean one' but saved-card proof was only a doc and conversation, and the reference Daniel asked for was never delivered.
Rep says 'I know' the Braintree call happened because questions changed, but it is inference; she also admits she is guessing what Braintree said.
Daniel is named as decider and signer, but rep says an unnamed engineer's prototype effectively won the deal, suggesting influence beyond Daniel.
Rep pitched a 'marketplace piece' and 'payouts' framing, while saying customers never use 'marketplace' or 'payouts'.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Rep answered 'Nothing, really. It was a clean one,' then admitted evasiveness on PayPal/Venmo and an undelivered saved-card reference when pressed.

outcome_signals.what: Daniel signed and finance signed what he brought; the deal appears won.
Customer moved from bake-off to no longer saying 'if' after the weekend prototype.
Open risks remained at kickoff (saved cards, Venmo); scope of what moved is not stated, so whether only part of the business moved is unclear.
